context: After forty days, the body was brought to the royal cemetery (the most important of which, according to Herodotus, was in a region called **Gerrhi** (GEHR-eye), probably in the lower Dnieper area) and placed in a large pit-chamber along with one of his wives (strangled), his cupbearer, his cook, his groom, his squire, and his messenger (all strangled), plus horses (strangled, arranged around the chamber in a circle), gold cups, weapons, and personal ornamen

Below Tabiti in the divine hierarchy were **Papaeus** (the sky father, equated by Herodotus with Zeus) and **Api** (the earth goddess), along with several other deities whose Scythian names and functions are only partially understood.
